$NBIS - our updated valuation after Q3

Nebius traded near $123 before the open after Q3. We cut revenue per active MW in our capacity model by about 10%, in line with peers like CoreWeave ($9–11m per MW).

Weighted value: ~$220 a share

Base: $271 (was $302)
• 1,750 MW active by end-2027 at $10.8m per MW
• FY2027 revenue of $12.4bn, inside the new $12–13bn outlook
• $6.3bn of FY2027 EBITDA at 16x; ~$4.1bn of equity raised through 2028

Bull: $343 (was $380)
• 2,100 MW, $15.6bn of revenue, and prepayments cover the build with no new equity

Bear: $54 (was $63)
• 1,300 MW and $8.1m per MW, so revenue lands at $7.8bn
• ~$17.5bn of equity raised at $95. Dilution, not EBITDA, drives this case.

What matters most
- Activation pace: every 250 MW is about $3bn of ARR
- Revenue per MW: new contracts at $20–25m per MW leave room above our base case
- Funding: $17–20bn of guided prepayments plus a new $3.5bn Citi facility
- Risk: capex guidance of ~$27bn for 2026 and $40–45bn for 2027 is above what our model assumes.

At ~$123, the market is pricing our bear case’s funding stress, not the base case’s operating path.

Sen. Kevin Cramer says Nvidia ($NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang should step down, citing national security and potential Chinese blackmail risks.

Growth is broadening
It’s no longer just memory. Growth is spreading across AI infrastructure and integrated memory. Penguin has managed 100K+ GPUs and 4.2bn GPU runtime hours, and that operating experience is the edge against OEMs and system integrators.

Services and software are the moat
• Customer contracts of 3–5 years with uptime SLAs
• ClusterWare monitors clusters and fixes issues automatically

Inference is a memory story
